names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 9 Οκτωβρίου, «Δικαίων Αβραάμ και Λωτ του ανεψιού του», with the rank word left off; the page's own heading for him is «Δικαιος Λωτ».
The bare name out of days.pravoslavie.ru's name page 1370, which is headed with the name alone, «Лот».

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 9. октобар ст. ст., „Св. праведни Аврам и Лот.“ — Св. is «saint» and not a rank, and праведни is the `righteous` this corpus puts in `types`, so both come off and the bare personal name, the second of the heading’s two, is the whole of the form. It is the same string this folder already stores as its `ru` form, the two calendars spelling the name identically; `foldchk.py` returns `[('lot', 'ru')]` for it and no other folder holds it.

source.text: days.pravoslavie.ru, 9 октября ст. ст. — «Прав. Авраама праотца и племянника его Лота (2000 до Р.Х.).»
source.note: No rank is read onto him. His line opens the day's second paragraph, which carries no icon; the day's two icons are both in the first, and belong to the apostle James and to Andronicus and his wife.

attestations.note: The Russian keeps him on the same day as the Greek and names him the same way, as Abraham's nephew. His index page keeps him on this one day, and the page it sends the reader to is the one he shares with Abraham — on this site as on saint.gr, he has no life of his own. The «(2000 до Р.Х.)» of the day line is an era and no `dates` are proposed from it.
Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (1 October 2026).

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 9ης Οκτωβρίου — «Δικαίων Αβραάμ και Λωτ του ανεψιού του»
Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 22.10.2026 (9. октобар ст. ст.) — „Св. праведни Аврам и Лот.“

attestations.note: The day’s third entry, and the second of the day’s two enumerated companies. The heading is quoted whole, **with the closing full stop the Prologue itself prints**, which is what BRIEF-SERBIAN §4 asks for. It had to be measured off the raw cached page, because `srbody.mjs` and `sr-cand.mjs` both strip it from their printed output: every heading of this day ends `. ` in the source. **An earlier wave of this reading quoted off the stripped output and wrote into its notes that the headings carry no closing stop, which the raw page contradicts for its own days as well as for these** — the rows of that wave are outside this reader’s range and are a finding for the author, not something fixed here. **A THIRD CALENDAR REFUSES TO GIVE HIM A LIFE, AND THAT IS THE FINDING.** The whole body of the entry is one sentence — „Читај о њему у књизи Постања.“, read about him in the book of Genesis. This folder already records that saint.gr and days.pravoslavie.ru both send the reader to Genesis rather than print a life, the Russian to chapters 12 to 25; the Ohrid Prologue does the same in one line, and for a man whose story is in the Pentateuch three calendars doing it is a decision and not a gap. Note that the heading names two and the body says о њему, about **him**, singular. THE HEADING ENUMERATES TWO AND ONLY ONE OF THEM TAKES A ROW FROM THIS DAY. §5 counts Аврам and Лот, two names and two folders; but `abraham-the-patriarch` **already carries a venerated `serbian` row, on the Julian 21 August**, with an `sr` form of its own. BRIEF-SERBIAN §1 is explicit that a saint who already holds a venerated `serbian` row from a different day is a reading for the report and never a draft, so he is left exactly as he is, and whether the Prologue’s 9 October should be recorded on that row as a second-day note is the author’s. `dates` UNTOUCHED, AND THERE IS NOTHING TO TOUCH: the folder holds `dates: null` and this entry prints no year, no reign and no scene. The appended paragraph carries no four-digit year. `types` UNTOUCHED at `righteous`, corroborated exactly by праведни in the heading. `related` UNTOUCHED: `abraham-the-patriarch` is already there, and the heading’s pairing is the only relation the entry asserts. No `locations`, no `office`. **THE FORM IS THE SAME STRING THIS FOLDER ALREADY HOLDS AS ITS RUSSIAN ONE** — `foldchk.py` returns `[('lot', 'ru')]` for «Лот» — so the `sr` form is written because this calendar prints it and nothing is folded across folders by it. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse. TWO OF THE DAY’S FIVE ENTRIES ARE REFUSED UNDER RULING 3 and are named here so that the next reader does not have to find them again. «Св. Димитрије патријарх Александријски», the eleventh bishop of Alexandria after Mark the Evangelist, who governed from 189 to 231 and in whose time Pantaenus of the catechetical school was sent to India and found there the Gospel Matthew had written in Hebrew: **forty-six folders are displayed as a Demetrius and not one of them is of Alexandria.** «Св. Стеван деспот српски», son of the despot Djuradj and Jerina, blinded at Adrianople with his brother Grgur, despot of Serbia from 1458, married to Angelina the daughter of Skanderbeg, dead in Italy in 1468 and lying at Krušedol: **fifty-four folders are displayed as a Stephen and not one of them is this despot, nor does the corpus hold Angelina, Grgur, Mara or the son Maximus named in the entry.** A person the Prologue names but no folder holds gets no folder from a reader, so both are a reading for the report and neither is in any prose.
